title: Elements and Compounds
seo_title: JSS 2 Intermediate Science: Elements and Compounds Worksheets (NERDC)
standard_code: JSS 2 Intermediate Science: Living and Non-Living Things
standard_text: Elements and compounds are pure substances; compounds are formed from elements in fixed ratios and represented by chemical formulas; physical and chemical properties. (summary of the Intermediate Science curriculum, JSS 2, theme: Living and Non-Living Things)
meta_desc: Free JSS 2 Intermediate Science worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: Living and Non-Living Things): pure substances and mixtures, physical and chemical properties, physical and chemical changes, chemical formulas and compounds in everyday products. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A compound is two or more elements chemically joined in a fixed ratio.
key_sub: The formula tells you which atoms and how many: H₂O has 2 H and 1 O.
body_html:
How to think about it

Matter is either a pure substance (an element or a compound) or a mixture. An element has only one kind of atom; a compound has two or more elements joined in a fixed ratio and can only be separated by a chemical change. Mixtures can be separated by physical means such as filtering or evaporating.

Physical properties (colour, density, melting point) can be observed without changing the substance; chemical properties (flammability, reaction with acid) describe how it changes into new substances. Signs of a chemical change include a new colour, a gas, a precipitate, light or a temperature change that is hard to reverse.

Example

How many atoms are in one molecule of glucose, C₆H₁₂O₆?

6 + 12 + 6

Answer: 24

Example

Is rusting iron a physical or a chemical change?

A new substance (iron oxide) forms.

Answer: chemical change

Common mistakes

  • Calling melting ice a chemical change.
  • Thinking a mixture of iron and sulfur is the compound iron sulfide.
  • Reading the subscript as applying to the atom before and after it (in CO₂ the 2 is for O only).

faq.q: Why must household cleaners never be mixed?
faq.a: Some mixtures, such as bleach with ammonia or acid, react to give toxic gases.

faq.q: What is the difference between an atom and a molecule?
faq.a: An atom is a single particle of an element; a molecule is two or more atoms joined together.

items.q: Is flour stirred into water a solution or a suspension?
items.e: A solution is clear and does not settle; a suspension is cloudy, its solid particles settle and can be filtered.

items.q: The formula of sulfur dioxide is SO<sub>2</sub>. How many oxygen atoms are in one molecule?
items.e: The small number after a symbol tells how many atoms of that element there are.

items.q: Which is a characteristic property that can help identify vegetable oil?
items.e: Density, melting point and boiling point do not depend on the amount, so they help identify a substance.

a chemical change, because a new substance forms
items.e: The substance is still the same; only its shape, size or state changed.

items.q: Dayo writes 4H<sub>2</sub>O. How many hydrogen atoms are there in all?
items.e: The coefficient 4 multiplies everything: 4 × 2 = 8.

items.q: Ibrahim writes 4CH<sub>4</sub>. How many hydrogen atoms are there in all?

items.q: Babatunde studies making ammonia: N2 + 3H2 → 2NH3. How many nitrogen atoms are in the reactants (left side)?
items.e: Multiply each coefficient by the subscript and add. The number is the same on both sides: 2.

items.e: Use the lowest numbers that make the total charge zero: 1 × (+2) + 2 × (−1) = 0.

items.q: Uju looks up calcium carbonate (chalk), CaCO<sub>3</sub>. How many atoms are in one molecule?

items.q: What kind of bond forms between zinc (Zn) and gold (Au)?

items.q: Turmeric solution is a natural indicator. What colour does it turn in soap solution (an alkali)?

items.q: What kind of bond forms between potassium (K) and nitrogen (N)?
